speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; please tell me, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That recent self-resolving knee pain and your camping trip in Minnesota are significant clues. Could you describe the appearance and location of the skin lesions, and do you have a history of tick bites or spider exposure?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP; REQUEST IMAGES: Lesion_photos, Wrist_X-ray

speaker: Doctor
text:
The joint aspiration revealing Gram-negative diplococci alongside a positive gonorrhea screen is highly specific. Given the migratory joint pain, fever, and the characteristic painful, purplish vesicular lesions on your wrists, this strongly points to a disseminated infection. Do you have a history of any other joint pain in recent weeks, and can you confirm the lesions are painful to the touch?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
